transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-06-17 09:30 PDT | Duration: 45m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Jared Collins (NovaPay Head of Platform), Priya Rao (NovaPay ML), Luis Gomez (NovaPay Infra)

Summary: quick sync on throughput results, tuning continuous batching, concurrency targets and queueing, and next steps for canary. Some audio artifacts and a few transcription errors (K V cache -> KV cache noted).

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, we did a short agenda: results from last week's run, Samir's tuning suggestions, customer questions on queueing and latency, and action items.
[00:18] Jared: yep, all good here. Priya, Luis with me.
[00:22] Priya: hi all.
[00:25] Samir: good morning. I'll start with the numbers we collected overnight; apologies one of the logs trimmed, so there's a small gap around the 3h mark.
[00:36] Samir: baseline run at 250 qps on the hosted config gave us about 12k tokens/sec aggregate, p50 ~45ms, p95 ~220ms, p99 ~480ms. We saw a tail at about 800ms on a couple of outliers when the KV cache miss rate spiked.
[00:54] Priya: when you say KV cash miss - was that cold start on the container reboots?
[01:00] Samir: sorta, yeah; looks like the cache eviction policy got triggered during a short burst which caused additional decode work. We're recommending adjusting the continuous batching buffer and increasing the cache retention TTL for the prefix cache.
[01:14] Maya: for context, their traffic has a lot of short requests and a small percent of long context ones, which hurts batching efficiency.
[01:22] Luis: our current infra does a fanout from the load balancer to many pods; we were hoping to hit 500 qps steady but worried about p99.
[01:30] Samir: two knobs: batching window and concurrency target. Right now batch window was 50ms, concurrency cap 16 per GPU. We suggested 30ms window and bump concurrency to 20 which increases per-batch size slightly and improves throughput at the cost of minimal added p50.
[01:48] Priya: does that change p99 much? Our user SLA is p99 < 500ms for the critical flows.
[01:55] Samir: with the 30ms/20 concurrency config we saw p95 ~200ms and p99 ~420ms in the lab for the synthetic traffic that matched your shape; real traffic will vary. We also recommend request queueing with a small head-of-line timeout to prevent long context requests from blocking short ones.
[02:16] Jared: queueing how? like prioritized queues?
[02:19] Samir: basic policy: short-only route goes to a hot path with tight batching and low queue wait time; long-context requests go to a separate pool or lower-priority queue. That can be done via routing rules in the Redwood config; you can also pin long jobs to Dedicated if you want isolation.
[02:35] Luis: curious on cost delta for Dedicated for the same throughput numbers. Maya?
[02:39] Maya: we'll send a pricing comparison but rough rule, Dedicated will have higher committed cost but gives predictable throughput and lower tail because of isolation. Hosted is cheaper for variable load. We'll put numbers in email.
[02:50] Priya: any thoughts on quantization to reduce token cost and maybe speed?
[02:54] Samir: yes, quantization helped in other pilots but it also changed quality slightly; for throughput we tested 4-bit quant on the model and saw ~10-15% CPU/GPU speedups but some regen differences. Recommend evals on your prompt set before applying to production.
[03:12] Jared: about autoscale - we saw some spikes that took a few minutes to scale up. Is there a recommended config to reduce impact?
[03:18] Samir: autoscale tuning: use a mix of reserved burst capacity and proactive scale triggers based on queue depth not just CPU. Redwood supports warm pools (pre-warmed containers) to reduce cold starts. Also you can configure minimum capacity to avoid scale-from-zero.
[03:31] Priya: okay that matches our concerns. For the steady 500 qps target, what's the recommended min capacity?
[03:36] Samir: depends on model size and GPU type; for your current model (approx 13B sharded) we'd recommend min 4 GPUs in the pool with autoscale to 8 for bursts, and a warm pool of one extra instance. That gave us steady results in our lab.
[03:51] Luis: any special networking needs for VPC peering? We have strict CIDR ranges.
[03:55] Maya: we'll share docs; typically it's standard VPC peering and egress rules, and we support private endpoints and SAML SSO. We'll include the KMS integration doc since you asked about encryption at rest.
[04:06] Priya: brief note: for our canary we want to validate both latency and output quality, so we need to run evals alongside throughput runs.
[04:12] Samir: yep, we can run a small eval harness on the pilot cluster; we'll flag quality regressions and tie to rollback.
[04:18] Jared: on the benchmark side we want a 24h run like you suggested; is there an existing script?
[04:23] Samir: yes I'll share the benchmark config + k6 script and the Docker image for the worker. Expect link in the follow-up. Note: one of last week's logs truncated because of the worker OOM, so we reconfigured memory limits.
[04:37] Priya: small question: who owns the SL A negotiation? our procurement will need numbers for committed capacity buy.
[04:43] Maya: I'll loop in account exec and we'll get a draft SLA and pricing; for now I'll provide the Dedicated delta.
[04:49] Luis: could we try the dedicated canary for an hour during low-traffic window, to validate tail behavior?
[04:55] Samir: that works; recommended: run the dedicated canary with same traffic profile and enable KV cache warming. We can do a 1h run first then escalate to 6h/24h.
[05:06] Maya: ok quick recap and action items...
[05:10] Maya: Samir will push updated image and bench config by Friday, Priya to send traffic shape and SLOs, Luis to share VPC CIDR, Maya will send pricing and security docs. We'll tentatively schedule the canary week of 6/22, pending your availability.
[05:28] Jared: thanks all, that timeline works, will confirm internally.
[05:31] Priya: thanks, bye.
[05:33] Samir: thanks. bye.

Notes about transcription: occasional mis-attributed lines and a few run-on sentences; some product names transcribed as 'K V cache' in places. References shared: benchmark-config.yaml (link shared in chat), k6-load-script.js (link), dedicated-pricing-sheet.xlsx (sent after call).

End of transcript.
